NEW DELHI: Congress leader Jairam Ramesh on Thursday questioned what he described as conflicting statements by senior military officials on the extent of cooperation between Pakistan and China during Operation Sindoor Sharing video clips on X, Ramesh said Deputy Chief of Army Staff Lt Gen Rahul Singh had, on July 4, 2025, highlighted what he called the “very disturbingly deep nature” of the Pakistan-China partnership during the military operation.The Congress leader contrasted those remarks with comments made by former Chief of Defence Staff Gen. Anil Chauhan on August 25, 2026, saying Chauhan's account appeared to be “simply opposite” to that of Lt. Gen. Singh.“On July 4 2025, the Deputy Chief of Army Staff Lt. Gen Rahul Singh had revealed the very disturbingly deep nature of the Pakistan-China jugalbandi during Operation Sindoor. On Aug 25, 2026, the former Chief of Defence Staff Gen. Anil Chauhan made his own revelations on this jugalbandi - which are simply opposite to what Lt. Gen Singh had said. The nation is confused," said Ramesh on X.The Congress leader questioned whether the differing accounts reflected a broader effort to shape the public narrative around India's relations with China.“What is going on here? Is there some deeper plan to change the narrative?” he asked.He also linked the issue to the Centre's broader China policy, alleging that there had been a “calibrated capitulation to China” and citing what he described as the Prime Minister's “infamous clean chit to China on June 2020” as well as India's record trade deficits with China.Ramesh's remarks came ex-CDS Chauhan, speaking at the ‘VIMARSH’ event on Operation Sindoor and its aftermath at the Vivekananda International Foundation, said Pakistan had failed to obtain evidence of the targets struck by India despite attempts to access commercial satellite imagery.Chauhan said the presence of Chinese personnel supporting Pakistan's military equipment during Operation Sindoor should be viewed in the context of "contractual obligations", while cautioning against drawing conclusions beyond established facts.In the clip shared by Ramesh, General Singh can be heard stating that the key lessons from Operation Sindoor were that India faced a multi-adversary challenge, with Pakistan at the forefront and China and Turkey providing significant military support. He added that China also used the conflict to assess its weapons and systems in a real-world environment.India launched Operation Sindoor on May 7, 2025, days after the April 22 Pahalgam terror attack that killed 26 people. The operation targeted terrorist infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoK).

Article Title: 'Took off for Kathmandu blissfully unaware': Shashi Tharoor on deadly Nepal floods
Article Text:
Tharoor said he was “blissfully unaware” of the devastation caused by a sudden flash flood in Nepal

Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Thursday said that he was “blissfully unaware” of the devastation caused by a sudden flash flood in Nepal’s Rasuwa district when he left for Kathmandu on Wednesday."A severe, sudden flash flood struck northern Nepal’s Rasuwa district near the Tibet border, causing widespread destruction along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. Global warming and/or an earthquake in Tibet may have caused a large chunk of a glacier to break off and fall into the valley below, experts surmise," Tharoor said in a post on X.Tharoor added that the flooding had destroyed at least 19 motorable bridges and washed away around 40 km of the Betrawati–Rasuwagadhi highway. Eight operational hydropower projects were also reported to have sustained heavy damage.Tharoor said he supported the Indian government’s immediate pledge of relief assistance to Nepal, adding that the country would need substantial help in responding to the destruction.He also expressed concern over the loss of life and those still missing, including Indians affected by the disaster."I fully support the Indian government’s immediate pledge of relief assistance.Nepal needs all the help it can get. My heart goes out to the victims and their loved ones, who include large numbers of Indian tourists, including a hundred performing the Kailash-Mansarovar Yatra. Prayers for the missing; may they be rescued soon," Tharoor said.The disaster has left at least 270 people dead and 826 missing in Nepal, while three people have died and 558 remain unaccounted for in Tibet, according to authorities.The scale of destruction has hampered rescue operations, with Nepalese officials reporting that dozens of bridges were destroyed and nearly 40 kilometres (25 miles) of roads damaged.The Nepalese Army launched helicopter operations on Thursday morning, rescuing more than 100 people from flood-affected areas, army spokesperson Brig. Gen. Raja Ram Basnet said. At least eight foreign nationals were also airlifted to Kathmandu, while army teams evacuated people trapped inside facilities associated with the Trishuli hydropower project.India is also coordinating efforts to assist its nationals stranded in the affected areas. Ministry of External Affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said five major groups, comprising around 288 Indian nationals, had been identified.“ The first group of 73 people who are working on the Trishuli-1 power project. Then, two separate groups of 37 and 49 nationals from Tamil Nadu, who traveled for Kailash Mansarovar Yatra through Samrat and Fly Everest Travels. There is a group of 32 Indian nationals from West Bengal who traveled with the help of Samrat Travels in Timure, which is in Rasuwa district.”“Then, a group of 61 Indian nationals from different states and then a group of 33 Indian nationals from Kerala. These are five major groups who comprise, by and large, 288 people that we are talking about,” he added.Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah and offered India’s assistance for rescue and relief operations.“India is prepared to provide Nepal with all possible types of humanitarian assistance,” PM Modi said, adding that Indian teams were coordinating rescue and relief efforts.The United Nations is also supporting the response, with agencies deploying personnel to assist local authorities. UN spokesperson Stephane Dujarric warned of a “massive humanitarian need” as rescue and relief operations continued.The disaster has also renewed concerns over the Himalayan region’s exposure to extreme weather events and glacial hazards, particularly in areas where difficult terrain and damaged infrastructure can complicate emergency response.
Article Summary: Tharoor said he was “blissfully unaware” of the devastation caused by a sudden flash flood in nepal on wednesday. The disaster has left at least 270 people dead and 826 missing in nepal, while three people have died and 558 remain unaccounted for in tibet.

Water rose 30 feet and at least 160 people were killed, while hundreds of others, including scores of Kailash Mansar-ovar pilgrims from India, remained missing after a flash flood and mudslide of unprecedented scale in Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers tore through a part of Nepal-Tibet border on Wednesday morning. It swept away settlements, hydropower units and the pilgrim route.Nepal Police put the toll at 157, while Chinese authorities reported three deaths and 265 people missing in Tibet’s Gyirong county. Nepal Police said 579 others — 466 foreigners from 28 countries and 113 Nepalis — remained untraced, including at least 133 Indians. Among the missing were at least 37 NRIs. Frighteningly, as many as 33 bodies were found 150km downstream at Chitwan, showing how far the dea-dly waters carried victims.Among the missing foreigners were 54 Americans, 34 Australians, 33 Britons, 24 Canadians, 19 Malaysians and 8 Koreans.Many were Kailash Mansarovar pilgrims, with nearly 400 of them, including the Indians, preparing to cross the Nepal-Tibet border or travelling through the region when the flood struck.Rescue personnel battled poor weather, mud, washed-out roads and high river levels even as authorities moved families from vulnerable settlements to safer locations.Nepal foreign minister Shisir Khanal told parliament that 29 police personnel and 44 soldiers remained untraced after floodwaters swept away their barracks in Rasuwa, while customs officials, hydropower workers and other employees stationed near the border were also missing. At the 20MW Langtang Khola Hydropower Project, dozens of workers are out of contact. The torrent also swept away or inundated security posts, customs facilities, banks and other establishments along the river corridor. Nepal PM Shah appealed for patience and unity as the Nepali Army, Nepal Police and Armed Police Force deployed helicopters, drones, boats and ground teams for search-and-rescue operations.Across the border, floods and mudslides severed several roads, communications and electricity around the (dry) Gyirong port, a key Nepal-Tibet crossing used by Kailash-Mansarovar pilgrims. Chinese president Xi Jinping called for “all-out efforts to search and rescue people who are missing”.The flood destroyed critical infrastructure across northern and central Nepal, with preliminary govt estimates showing at least 19 bridges and around 40 km of roads damaged or washed away; 13 hydropower projects were hit, and around 200 trucks were lost. The Nepal govt declared the worst-affected areas disaster-hit zones for the next 3 months and ordered authorities to provide free treatment to the injured.

Article Title: India & China announce 8-point boundary consensus before Xi's visit, target early & substantial harvest in border delimitation
Article Text:
According to the joint statement, both sides agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India and China jointly announced Wednesday that the Special Representatives (SR) dialogue on the boundary question - co-chaired by Ajit Doval and Wang Yi this week - had led to an 8-point consensus, signalling some positive progress in boundary talks ahead of President Xi Jinping's visit to India next month.These included advancing consultations for an "early and substantial harvest" of boundary delimitation, setting up more meeting points and hotlines to improve border management, improving understanding of LAC and addressing ground situation through diplomatic and military engagements, expanding trans-border trade and rivers cooperation. The consensus was announced in a rare joint statement after the SR talks.Building upon the outcomes from the last round of talks in 2024, the 2 sides agreed that the Expert Group on Boundary Delimitation and Working Group on Border Management would advance discussions on an “Early and Substantial Harvest” of boundary delimitation and Border Management. The first task for both these groups would be to agree on their respective Terms of Reference, said the joint statement.India and China had agreed last year to set up an expert group under the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on India-China Border Affairs (WMCC), to explore early harvest in boundary delimitation in the India-China border areas.The formulation was changed to early and substantial on this occasion.Two additional meeting points for military talks and 2 more channels of border military hotlines in the Eastern and Middle Sectors were agreed upon to reinforce border management measures, according to both sides.“The two sides underlined their commitment to advancing negotiations on a framework for the settlement of the boundary question in accordance with the Agreement on Political Parameters and Guiding Principles for Settlement of the India-China Boundary Question signed in 2005 and the consensus reached in subsequent SR Talks in pursuit of a fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable solution,” said the MEA in a statement. Unlike the Chinese readout of the talks on Tuesday, the joint statement did not mention package settlement or solution, although the 2005 agreement talks about making adjustments to reach a package settlement.The two sides also reaffirmed their commitment to upholding the guidance received from Modi and Xi, maintaining peace and tranquility in the border areas and creating an atmosphere for healthy and steady development of bilateral relations.According to the joint statement, both sides agreed that any situation on the ground would be addressed promptly through existing diplomatic and military channels, including the WMCC, local commander‑level meetings and other agreed mechanisms, to resolve outstanding issues and avoid misunderstanding and miscalculation along the LAC. “The two sides discussed ways to improve understanding of LAC in appropriate areas, for better border management,” said the joint statement.Both sides also noted the progress on trans-border cooperation, with the Indian side appreciating the efforts made by the Chinese side to increase the number of batches of Indian official pilgrimage Kailash-Manasarovar Yatra (KMY) in the Tibet Autonomous Region of China.“Both sides appreciated the reopening of the three designated border trading points. The two sides agreed to strengthen exchanges and cooperation in border trade, pilgrimage and other areas, with the view to work together to create an atmosphere featuring dialogue, peace, consultation and cooperation in the border areas,” said the joint statement.India and China also agreed to hold the next meeting of the India-China Expert-Level Mechanism on Trans-border Rivers in September and maintain communication on issues including hydrological data sharing, and renewal of the relevant MoUs. It’s important for India that China shares hydrological information during emergency situations based on humanitarian considerations. The two sides agreed to hold the 26th round of SR Talks in India in 2027.
Article Summary: India and china announced wednesday that the special representatives (sr) dialogue on the boundary question had led to an 8-point consensus. The consensus was announced in a rare joint statement after the sr talks. The two sides agreed to hold the 26th round of sr talks in india in 2027.

NEW DELHI: Less than two months after retirement as the IAF's vice chief, Air Marshal Nagesh Kapoor (Retd) has slammed the delay in the delivery of Tejas (LCA) fighter jet by Hindustan Aeronautics Limited to the air force, saying, “why must it be that a machine that was promised to us so many years back with a certain set of capabilities continues to be denied to us on one pretext or the other”.In an interview to NDTV, the IAF veteran said, “Why must we be hamstrung because someone somewhere has not been able to keep their promises?”The delivery of the indigenous LCA Tejas Mk1A jets by HAL to the IAF has faced multi-year delays, primarily caused by late supplies of F404-IN20 engines by American GE company, complex mission software validation, and stringent operational requirements set by the IAF.When asked if advanced Tejas Mk-2 may be operationally relevant when it starts entering service in big numbers in mid 2030s at a time when China is already raising its fleet of its 5th-generation fighter jet, the former vice-chief said, “No, operationally, definitely no.”With China on its way to deploying 500 5th-generation J-20 fighters by 2030, India is still struggling to get the delivery of the first squadron by 4.5-generation Tejas Mk1A. Though the IAF had placed orders for a total of 180 Tejas Mk1A fighter jets long ago, HAL hopes to deliver the first 18-25 Tejas Mk1A only by March 2027.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) did not totally rule out the role of Tejas Mk2 in future when he said, “You can have a certain number of those 5th generation and 6th generation fighters, but given the size of the country, you won't be able to deploy them everywhere.So those gaps which continue to remain to be filled will have to be filled by this class of aircraft.” “I want Tejas Mk-2 to come, I want India’s 5th-gen AMCA to come. But they must come at a much faster speed,” he said.When asked about Russia’s 5th-gen fighter jet Su-57, the former vice-chief said when the Russian fighter is compared to western jets like American F-35, western jets have an edge over the Su-57 as they have better avionics and stealth.Air Marshal Kapoor (Retd) suggested that India should partner with an European consortium working on state-of-the-art sixth generation platforms. “There are other things that are happening — why not join FCAS (Future Combat Air System is the European programme for 6th generation jet under development by French Dassault Aviation, Airbus and Indra Sistemas) Why not GCAP (Global Combat Air Programme is a multinational initiative led by Italy, Japan, and UK to jointly develop a sixth-generation jet).“'You are probably going with a consortium which has got a good record of delivery, of development. Why go through this Gen 4, Gen 4.5 steps when you know the next best thing is already being thought of and why not just join up there?,” the IAF veteran said.His comments underline the difficult choices facing India’s air power planners: meeting immediate squadron requirements while ensuring that indigenous programmes do not fall behind the rapid evolution of military aviation technology.
Article Summary: Air marshal kapoor (retd) did not totally rule out the role of tejas mk2 in future. He suggested that india should partner with an european consortium working on state-of-the-art sixth generation platforms. His comments underline the difficult choices facing india’s air power planners.

Article Title: COP17: New global architecture for drought resilience launched at UNCCD meet
Article Text:
(Representative image) DR’s technical monitoring metrics will enable countries to assess their capacity to anticipate, prepare for and adapt to drought (Photo: Reuters).

NEW DELHI: Amid reports that three out of four people worldwide could face drought by 2050, the United Nations Convention to Combat Desertification (UNCCD) during its 17th conference (COP17) on Wednesday took a significant step in advancing new global architecture for drought resilience by showcasing the world's first Drought Resilience Index (DRI) and launching the Drought Resilience Investment Facility (DRIF) to help countries strengthen their drought resilience.DR’s technical monitoring metrics will enable countries to assess their capacity to anticipate, prepare for and adapt to drought while identifying vulnerabilities and informing more effective policies and investments. It’s a new AI-powered features that can help policy-makers, technical experts and the public interpret complex data and turn it into practical insights.On the other hand, DRIF - the first global catalytic financing platform dedicated to drought resilience - will use public capital to reduce investment risks and unlock much larger flows of institutional and private finance for projects that strengthen water security, sustainable agriculture, nature-based solutions and land restoration.“COP17 is about turning commitments into implementation. We now have stronger financing mechanisms, better tools and practical guidance to help countries prepare for drought before it becomes a crisis,” said UNCCD executive secretary Yasmine Fouad.“The task now is to connect these pieces and put them to work at scale, through governments, development partners, financial institutions and the private sector,” she added.India, represented by a team led by Union environment minister Bhupende Yadav at COP17, too advocated for strengthening drought resilience. Yadav on Tuesday called for a fundamental shift in the global approach to drought from “reactive relief to proactive technology-enabled resilience”.Underlining India’s core belief that “drought must be managed as a predictable, preventable risk, and not a recurring disaster demanding emergency response”, the minister said, “Preparedness over response, prevention over crisis management, resilience over recovery should be the goal.”
Article Summary: The united nations convention to combat desertification (unccd) on wednesday took a significant step in advancing new global architecture for drought resilience. The unccd showcased the world's first drought resilience index (dri) and launched the d drought resilience investment facility (drif) dr’s technical monitoring metrics will enable countries to assess their capacity to anticipate, prepare for and adapt to drought.

NEW DELHI: With obesity, particularly among children, turning out to be a major health concern and number of overweight school-going kids and adolescents increasing from 2% to 10% between 2000 and 2022, Supreme Court has indicated that the health of people cannot be compromised and sent an ultimatum to Centre to implement its order for putting front-of-pack warning labels on junk food.“If the Union does it on its own, well and good, otherwise we shall proceed to pass further directions ...We do not approve the stance of the Union when it says it is not possible to match with international standards, more particularly, developed countries. Should India remain as an underdeveloped country? That’s the question we are putting forward for the Union to consider,” a bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said in its order, as it linked the issue of food safety to right of life guaranteed under Article 21.The order, in response to a PIL filed by NGO ‘3S and Our HEALTH Society’ which moved SC through advocate Rajiv Shankar Dvivedi, comes as govt has seemed reluctant to implement front-of-pack warning labels on junk food. SC said food with high salt, sugar, saturated fat and calories could lead to health risks and clearer nutrition information must be displayed to help to make healthier choices. As per Economic Survey 2025-26, India’s ultra-processed food market increased by more than 150% between 2009 and 2023, while obesity reportedly doubling.

Article Title: 'Open dialogue, inclusive to all': RSS reacts to row over Mohan Bhagwat's New York event
Article Text:
RSS chief Mohan Bhagwat will address the 'Universal Oneness Celebration' at Madison Square Garden on August 29.

Interfaith forum

A major RSS outreach event is being planned in New York, with Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat scheduled to address the "Universal Oneness Celebration" at Madison Square Garden on August 29.The event is being organised by American Hindus for Engagement and Dialogue and is expected to bring together Hindu-American organisations and members of the Indian diaspora around the themes of shared heritage, interfaith dialogue and unity.The programme, however, has triggered a political controversy even before it takes place, with New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani publicly opposing Bhagwat’s appearance.Mamdani, New York’s first Muslim and Indian-American mayor, said he did not support the planned rally, describing the RSS’s vision as exclusionary and contrasting it with his own understanding of India as a pluralistic country. At the same time, he acknowledged that the event is privately organised and said he was unsure whether the city had the legal authority to cancel it.The controversy is particularly significant because of Mamdani’s own Indian heritage and his position as mayor of one of the world's most diverse cities.His criticism has also drawn support from groups opposed to the RSS, while critics of the mayor have questioned whether his position amounts to singling out a Hindu organisation.The RSS, meanwhile, has pushed back strongly against the criticism.RSS communications chief Sunil Ambekar said the New York gathering represents an interfaith forum where Bhagwat will engage with a “diverse, multicultural, and multi-faith audience”.He said the event reflects what the RSS describes as the inclusive and welcoming nature of the Bharatiya ethos, and invited anyone interested in understanding the organisation’s philosophy to participate in open dialogue.The timing of Bhagwat’s visit is also important. The RSS is marking its centenary in 2025-26, and the New York programme forms part of a broader international outreach by Bhagwat covering the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom. The stated objective is to engage Indian-origin communities abroad and present the RSS’s views on India, Hindu society and its own philosophy.
Article Summary: Rss chief mohan bhagwat will address the 'universal oneness celebration' at madison square garden on august 29. The event is being organised by american hindus for engagement and dialogue. It is expected to bring together hindu-american organisations and members of the indian diaspora around the themes of shared heritage, interfaith dialogue and unity.

NEW DELHI: India has called on the international community to work collectively to safeguard critical sea lanes and maritime infrastructure, saying secure and predictable shipping routes are essential to ensure the uninterrupted movement of food, fertilisers, fuel and other vital commodities amid conflicts and growing disruptions to global supply chains.Speaking at a UN Security Council high-level open debate on Tuesday on the theme ‘Food Under Fire: The Security Council's Role in Mitigating Global and Local Food Crises’, India’s Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, said regional conflicts were increasingly producing consequences far beyond the immediate theatres of hostilities.“Secure and predictable maritime trade routes are indispensable for the uninterrupted movement of food, fertilisers, fuel and other essential commodities," Parvathaneni said, underscoring the need to preserve the safety and freedom of navigation for commercial shipping in accordance with international law.The call comes as conflicts and attacks on key maritime routes continue to threaten global food and energy supplies. UN secretary general Antonio Guterres told the Council that the Strait of Hormuz carries around a fifth of global oil supplies and a third of global fertiliser trade.“Restrictions and closures have driven up commodity prices and made availability plummet. And attacks on commercial vessels in the Red Sea are further threatening supply chains for food and other commodities,” Guterres said.Parvathaneni warned that disruptions to commercial shipping during conflicts could have cascading effects well beyond the affected region, with food-importing developing countries and humanitarian operations bearing a disproportionate burden.“The international community must therefore work collectively to safeguard critical sea lanes and maritime infrastructure, while ensuring that legitimate commercial trade and humanitarian shipments are able to proceed without undue impediment,” he said.India said the immediate priority for the Security Council should be to reduce the humanitarian consequences of conflicts by facilitating safe, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access, supporting de-confliction arrangements where appropriate and ensuring that Council measures, including sanctions regimes, do not inadvertently obstruct humanitarian assistance or legitimate food and agricultural trade.Parvathaneni also called for timely assessments of disruptions to critical supply chains covering food, fertiliser, fuel and humanitarian logistics, drawing on the expertise of the food and agriculture organisation, the World Food Programme and other relevant agencies.“Such assessments must remain objective, evidence-based and free from politicisation,” he said.The envoy said food insecurity was fundamentally a consequence of conflict, political instability and underdevelopment, rather than their root cause. He called for greater cooperation among member states, international financial institutions, regional organisations and development partners to strengthen domestic agricultural production, diversify supply chains and improve storage and logistics infrastructure.“Predictable and affordable access to fertilisers, quality seeds, technology and concessional finance remains indispensable, particularly for developing countries. Open, transparent and rules-based trade in food and agricultural inputs also remains critical to global food security,” he said.India also cautioned against “over-reliance " on any single model of production, arguing that such dependence could leave food systems vulnerable to geopolitical disruptions, economic coercion and weaponisation.“We must encourage small and marginal farmers to enhance their productivity and contribute to ensuring food security in developing countries of the Global South. We must also encourage climate-resilient crops such as millets rather than limit conceptions of food security to the biggest staple, grain crops such as rice, wheat and corn,” Parvathaneni said.Guterres said 2025 saw the highest number of armed conflicts since World War II alongside some of the highest levels of global acute hunger on record, with at least 266 million people facing acute food insecurity.He described the simultaneous confirmation of famine in Sudan and Gaza in 2025 as a “shameful milestone”, adding that conflict and violence were the primary drivers of hunger in 12 of the 13 hunger hotspots of greatest concern identified in the UN’s latest Hunger Hotspots report.
Article Summary: India has called on the international community to work collectively to safeguard critical sea lanes and maritime infrastructure. The call comes as conflicts and attacks on key maritime routes continue to threaten global food and energy supplies.

Article Title: India vs China: How their nuclear-capable missile arsenals compare
Article Text:
The Agni family of missiles are designed to carry the weight of India's strategic weapons. (Image credit: DRDO)

Indian and Chinese strategic missiles

China and India, Asia's two most powerful countries, have spent decades building ballistic missile arsenals. These ballistic missiles are strategic weapons that act as a deterrent, under the concept of Mutually Assured Destruction (MAD). This prohibitive concept states that two nuclear armed powers will not use these weapons on each other, as the use of such a weapon will ensure a retaliatory strike, thereby increasing the cost for the attacker. India and China's strategic missile arsenals now bear resemblance, but also at the same time there are differences in capability. The two countries also are also employing different philosophies for the use of these weapons, as the US Naval Institute states that China is building a significant amount of missile capability to hit US bases in the vast Pacific.While India is building its strategic missile arsenal to act as an insurance against attacks from nuclear weapons armed entities. This concept is enshrined in India's no first use policy for nuclear weapons. India depends on the Agni family of missiles for its land based nuclear deterrence, while China depends on the Dongfeng series.At the shorter end of the spectrum, China's road-mobile DF-16 offers a range between 800 and 1,000 kilometres, giving it reach over Taiwan and much of the western Pacific.India's comparable system, the Agni-I, delivers a range of 700 to 900 kilometres, and while it lacks the DF-16's higher payload capacity of up to 1,500 kilograms, it remains a reliable, road and rail-mobile system tailored specifically for shorter-range contingencies closer to India's borders.Moving up the ladder in terms of range and capability, China's DF-21, one of the People's Liberation Army's most storied missiles, offers a range of up to 2,500 kilometres and famously spawned the world's first anti-ship ballistic missile variant, the DF-21D. India's Agni-II sits in a similar bracket, with a declared range of 2,000 to 3,500 kilometres, and has long been described as central to India's deterrence posture with respect to China, despite New Delhi's insistence that its missile programme is not aimed at any single adversary.At the intermediate range, China's DF-26, capable of striking targets over 5,000 kilometres away, including American bases in Guam, sits close in class to India's Agni-III, which offers a declared range of 3,000 to 5,000 kilometres and has been noted for a circular error probable of just around 40 metres, making it among the most accurate missiles in its class. This accuracy allows India to rely on smaller-yield warheads while still achieving high lethality, a design philosophy that keeps the system relatively compact for its range class.Where the comparison becomes genuinely interesting is at the intercontinental tier. China's DF-31A, a solid-fuel ICBM, boasts a range in excess of 11,000 kilometres. India's Agni-V, its first genuine intercontinental system, offers a declared range of 7,000 to 8,000 kilometres, though some Chinese analysts have suggested its true reach may extend closer to 8,000 kilometres once payload adjustments are factored in. Both missiles share canisterised, road-mobile configurations, a design choice that improves survivability and reduces launch preparation time.At the very top sits China's DF-41, believed to carry ten to twelve MIRV warheads across a range of 12,000 to 15,000 kilometres, making it one of the longest-range missiles in the world. India's answer, the still-developing Agni-VI, is expected to offer a comparable range of as much as 10,000 kilometres, with reports suggesting it could eventually be fitted with MIRV warheads and even a submarine-launched variant, mirroring China's own efforts to build a survivable, multi-domain nuclear triad.Taken together, the comparison suggests India has broadly kept pace with China across most range categories, even as Beijing continues to hold an edge in payload flexibility, warhead multiplicity, and the sheer scale of its overall missile inventory.
Article Summary: China and india have spent decades building ballistic missile arsenals. These ballistic missiles act as a deterrent, under the concept of mutually assured destruction (mad) china is building a significant amount of missile capability to hit us bases in the pacific.

Why she keeps returning to this story

A fan question on Kylie Kelce's podcast turned into one of her most honest moments yet. Asked point-blank if she'd been scared to try for another baby after her 2018 miscarriage, the mom of four didn't hedge, she confirmed the fear was real, and it stuck around a lot longer than most people would expect.Kelce first went public with the loss last October, during Pregnancy and Infant Loss Awareness Month, explaining that a doctor's visit before the birth of her eldest daughter, Wyatt, confirmed there was no heartbeat.The timing made it worse, the diagnosis fell on her husband Jason's birthday, and she initially couldn't bring herself to break the news to him that day. This week's episode picked up the thread from a different angle: what actually happened once she and Jason decided to try again.According to Kelce, getting pregnant with Wyatt didn't erase the anxiety, it just reshaped it. In early pregnancy, she found herself checking survival odds on a near-weekly basis, and by the later stages of her second trimester, that worry shifted into wondering whether a baby born that day could make it. She's been candid that this obsessive tracking wasn't necessarily a healthy habit, just one that helped her get through it, and one that carried into her later pregnancies too.Kelce didn't have to revisit this topic; she's already raising four young daughters, and the loss happened years ago.But her reasoning for continuing to talk about it is straightforward. She views grief from pregnancy loss as something with no real end date, capable of resurfacing unexpectedly no matter how much time has passed or how many kids follow.It's a theme she's returned to more than once, and each time she's shared it, she's said the response from others tends to be more stories of loss rather than awkward silence.She was careful not to frame the fear as the end of the story, either. Her bottom line was that avoiding the risk entirely would have meant never having Wyatt at all, so for her, moving forward despite the fear was worth it. It's a message that fits her reputation for being unusually direct about hard topics, and one she's now delivered twice, in two different ways, likely for the benefit of anyone quietly sitting with the same fear.

Article Title: Quote of the day by King Charles: "To my darling Mama, as you begin your last great journey to join my dear…" - a tribute to Queen Elizabeth, on gratitude, service and a son's farewell
Article Text:

Quote of the day by King Charles

"To my darling Mama, as you begin your last great journey to join my dear late Papa, I want simply to say this: Thank you. Thank you for your love and devotion to our family and to the family of nations you have served so diligently all these years. May flights of angels sing thee to thy rest"

What is the meaning of King Charles' quote

Why King Charles thanked Queen Elizabeth II

The personal meaning behind "my darling Mama"

What "the family of nations" actually means

Why Charles' farewell centred on service

The Shakespeare reference at the end of the speech

How the quote reflects the relationship between duty and family

How to apply the message in daily life

Some other memorable quotes by King Charles

"I am a dangerous person because I mind about things."

"It is important to be able to stand back and see the bigger picture."

"The environment is something that is very close to my heart."

"I think we have to be very careful about what we do to the natural world."

Few words spoken at a moment of personal loss carry the weight of an entire lifetime. When Queen Elizabeth II died on 8 September 2022, her eldest son, King Charles III, addressed the nation the following day, speaking as both a new monarch and a grieving son at the same time. Recorded in the Blue Drawing Room at Buckingham Palace, with a framed portrait of his mother resting on the desk beside him, his tribute combined personal affection, real gratitude and a recognition of her extraordinary decades of public service. It became one of the most widely remembered moments of that entire period, quoted on front pages across the country the following morning. For millions watching, the address offered a rare glimpse behind the crown, where duty and private grief briefly occupied space. His carefully chosen words also captured the enormous responsibility that had suddenly passed to him, making the moment deeply personal and historically significant.The speech also reassured a grieving public that the values associated with Elizabeth’s reign would continue, while Charles acknowledged the changes that lay ahead. His measured tone reflected both continuity and transition as Britain entered a new chapter.The address also marked the beginning of a new constitutional era, as Charles formally assumed the role his mother had held for seven decades. His message balanced continuity with change, reassuring the public while acknowledging the profound personal loss.At its heart, the message is about gratitude, love and farewell. Charles begins by describing his mother's death as a "last great journey," a gentle way of naming the end of a life, before referring directly to her reunion with her late husband, Prince Philip, who had died in April 2021. Rather than dwelling on the enormous constitutional change actually taking place, Charles places his mother's role firmly within a family context first. He thanks her for the love and devotion she gave to her family, before widening that same gratitude to the people and nations she served. The simplicity of the words "thank you," repeated before he expands on what he is actually grateful for, turns the tribute into an expression of appreciation for an entire lifetime of service.Queen Elizabeth II became monarch in 1952 and remained on the throne for more than seven decades, making her the longest-reigning monarch in British history. Across that period, she served under fifteen British prime ministers and witnessed enormous political, social and technological change. For Charles, though, her significance was never limited to her constitutional role alone. She was also, simply, his mother. His tribute moves between these two identities throughout, recognising her commitment to the "family of nations" she served while speaking about her in the deeply personal language of a son saying goodbye to his parent.The phrase "my darling Mama" gave the speech a genuinely intimate quality that stood apart from the formal language normally associated with royal addresses. Charles was speaking to a global audience, and yet the words themselves were directed towards one single person. Calling his mother "Mama" reflected the private family relationship sitting behind the public institution. Elizabeth II had been Queen to millions of people, but to her son she remained, simply, his mother. That contrast is really what gave the tribute its personal weight rather than letting it feel purely ceremonial.Charles' reference to the "family of nations" reflects Queen Elizabeth II's role across the Commonwealth, a voluntary association of independent countries, many with historical connections to the British Empire, of which she served as Head throughout her entire reign. Her role involved maintaining relationships with leaders and people across every member country, while representing a genuine continuity through decades of political change. Describing these countries as a "family of nations" highlighted exactly the relationships his mother had worked to maintain across the whole of her reign.A central theme running through Queen Elizabeth II's public life was duty. In her 1952 accession broadcast, she pledged her life to the service of the people of the United Kingdom and the Commonwealth. Seven decades later, Charles' farewell returned directly to that same idea. Describing her as having served "so diligently all these years" recognised both the length and the sheer consistency of that commitment. It also reflected the unusual nature of her reign specifically, since she continued carrying out official duties well into her nineties, including appointing Liz Truss as prime minister only two days before her death.Charles closed his tribute with the words "May flights of angels sing thee to thy rest." The line comes from William Shakespeare's Hamlet, Act 5, Scene 2, spoken by Horatio as he mourns his friend at the play's close, "Now cracks a noble heart. Good night, sweet prince, and flights of angels sing thee to thy rest." The reference gave Charles' speech a genuinely literary and solemn conclusion, connecting his personal farewell to one of the most recognisable expressions of grief in English literature, and its suggestion of a peaceful passage into rest made it particularly fitting for a speech delivered the day after losing a parent.One of the most powerful aspects of Charles' tribute is how it brings together two sides of Queen Elizabeth II's life at once, a mother within her own family, and a monarch with responsibilities reaching far beyond it. Charles' words acknowledge both directly, first thanking her for her "love and devotion to our family," then expanding that same gratitude outward to the people and nations she served. Say thank you while you still can, since the people who matter most should never have to wait for a farewell to hear how much they are actually appreciated. Recognise quiet, unglamorous forms of service, since care and responsibility are often given without much recognition at all. Value family relationships alongside professional achievement, and remember that simple words of love and appreciation tend to become more meaningful, not less, with time.Why King Charles' farewell remains memorableCharles' first address as King carried an unavoidable constitutional significance, and yet its most memorable passage was deeply personal. He was not simply acknowledging the end of a historic reign. He was saying goodbye to the woman who had been his mother for more than seven decades. The repeated "thank you" captures the central emotion of the entire tribute. After a lifetime defined by public duty, Charles chose to close his first address as monarch with something considerably more private, a reminder that behind every title and institution sits an ordinary human relationship. A queen can be a constitutional figure to an entire nation while remaining, simply, "Mama" to her own son.
